messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Fixes for Chromosome Explorer in Firefox 9, IE 7, and Safari 5
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

thanks for this. This is great! Your proof-of-concept that it works in
other browser with only minor changes made me look into this in more
detail and I discovered the reasons for it not working before.

Everyone, I've updated to ChromosomeExplorer v3.3 which seems to work
in most browsers, e.g.

http://aroma-project.org/demos/

To generate your own ChromosomeExplorer v3.3 reports, you'll need to
update to aroma.core v2.4.4 or newer;

source("http://aroma-project.org/hbLite.R");
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix");

If you already have generated some ChromosomeExplorer reports, you
need to override them using setup(ce, force=TRUE), e.g.

ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(...);
setup(ce, force=TRUE);

When time permits, I'll also update ArrayExplorer (which still only
works in Firefox 3.x).

Cheers,

Henrik

On Tue, Jan 31, 2012 at 9:39 AM, Keith Ching <keith...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I don't know if this has been fixed already, but I found a simple
> solution (hack) to allow Chromosome Explorer to be used with Firefox 9.01
> IE7, and Safari 5. ( I have not tested other versions.)
>
> For some reason, the order of loading the js script files is different.. so
> the explorer obj is undef when onLoad is being defined.
>
> So if you init the explorer obj here first, it seems to work
>
> ###############
> edit
> reports/includes/js/ChromosomeExplorer3.1/main.js
>
> remove line 1
> var explorer = new ChromosomeExplorer();
>
> in each dir for data edit (eg)
> reports/PDX/cbs/ChromosomeExplorer.onLoad.js
>
> add to the top
>
> var explorer = new ChromosomeExplorer();
>
> ############
>
> in addition, for IE
>
> Edit reports/includes/js/domUtils.js
>
> When setting the contents of the span, FF will interpret HTML
> while IE will use plain text.
>
> Change the method to set as HTML
>
> function updateLabel(id, text) {
>   var obj = document.getElementById(id);
>   //DOM_setInnerText(obj, text); /* From Webcuts.js */
>   obj.innerHTML = text;
> }
>
>
> Keith Ching

reported the error at this point… :-$

Hi,

I've uploaded aroma.core v2.4.5 which now includes the missing
require.js file.  In a *fresh R session* (R -vanilla), do:

source("http://aroma-project.org/hbLite.R");
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix");

When doing setup(ce, force=TRUE), with 'ce' being an(y)
ChromosomeExplorer object, it will update:

(i) the ./reports/includes/ directory structure, which is used by
*all* ChromosomeExplorer reports, and
(ii) the two files ChromosomeExplorer.html and
ChromosomeExplorer.onLoad.js that is specific to actual report.

DETAILS: Note that ChromosomeExplorer.html is the same for all reports
and it is only ChromosomeExplorer.onLoad.js that is unique to each
report.  Thus, if you wish to update previous reports, Step (i) is
only needed once, and Step (ii) is needed for each data set/report.
There is nothing else that have changed.

About Firefox 3.6/IE8: It appears that ChromosomeExplorer v3.3 is not
working with Firefox 3.6 or Internet Explorer 8.  Whereas it should be
ok to skip backward compatibility with Firefox 3.6, I think IE8 should
still be supported.  Hopefully this should be possible to solve.
However, it's way better that we can now support new browser instead
of just Firefox 3.6.  I understand that people want to have something
that works with everything, especially since you like me have old
reports sitting around.

The demos on http://aroma-project.org/demos/ are using
ChromosomeExplorer v3.3.  Yes, as others concluded, the
ChromosomeExplorer reports are pure HTML, Javascript and lots of PNG
image files and are independent of R in the sense that as soon as they
are generated R is not needed.  These reports are designed such that
they should be display via the local file system (file://) as well as
via a webserver (http://).

Finally, major releases of aroma.* (e.g. v2.3.0, v2.4.0 and v2.5.0)
are the best tested ones where I run major 24h redundancy tests,
whereas intermediate releases (e.g. v2.4.5) are either bug fixes or
beta releases and these do not undergo the same scrutiny.  So, expect
some shaky rides with the latter.  It is always possible to go back
and reinstall previous "stable" releases, by installing manually from
CRAN.

Thanks for all the useful feedback

/Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi Irsan,

so a quick background: (i) it is important that document is in sync
with the software and not outdated, (ii) it is very time consuming to
make sure is the case, and (iii) even more so to provide rich/detailed
documentation.  Since there are very limited resources, the strategy
in aroma is to at least keep docs in sync with code and not adding to
much extra documentation that risk to be outdated when software gets
updated.  Large parts of the help pages you find are automatically
generated from code, which helps in this sense.  Because of this, the
source code is ultimately the best documentation, but I understand
that that may be tricky to follow.

It may also be useful to know that the aroma framework exists for a
few reasons: (a) to provide the research community with a toolbox
allowing for standard analyzes as well as for developing new
statistical methods, (b) to share make our analysis methods (CRMAv2,
FIRMA, PSCBS, ...) easily available to everyone, and (c) to make it
possible for ourselves (authors/collaborators of aroma authors) to be
able develop additional methods.  When it comes to solid
documentation, we prioritize (b) first and then (a).

You may already know this, but some important clarification about the
R terminology, which, if used when reporting issues here and to the R
help and the Bioconductor help mailing lists, simplifies the
troubleshooting:

- Warnings and errors: R generates warnings and errors.  Errors often
stops the running of your scripts/code, whereas warnings are less
severe and are only reported as messages.
- Crashes/core dumps: When people talk about crashes (or core dumps in
the Unix world), they mean that something really severe happened
causing R to simply die and shutdown by itself without user
interaction.

> source code is ultimately the best documentation, but I understand

> It may also be useful to know that the aroma framework exists for a
> few reasons: (a) to provide the research community with a toolbox
> allowing for standard analyzes as well as for developing new
> statistical methods, (b) to share make our analysis methods (CRMAv2,
> FIRMA, PSCBS, ...) easily available to everyone, and (c) to make it

> able develop additional methods.  When it comes to solid

Hi,

On Fri, Feb 17, 2012 at 1:44 PM, Michelle <suy...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Henrik,
>
> I ran the PSCBS package on some Affy SNP 6.0 arrays. In the output I found
> that several files contain a few lines of negative "tcnMean" values, while
> the rest are all positive. My question is - the total copy number is
> supposed to be positive, right? Are these negative values caused by some
> error in the computation? If so, how to adjust them?

yes, *true*/*biological* CNs cannot be negative.  However,
*observed*/*estimated* ones may very well end up being *slightly*
negative, due to noise in data.  So, it is neither a bug nor something
wrong with PSCBS.

There is nothing in Paired PSCBS that enforces the CNs to be strictly
non-negative (>= 0), neither does it restrict the CN estimates to be
integers (0, 1, 2, 3, ...), because there may be normal cell
contamination or tumor clonality.  However, you can imagine that there
are downstream methods that takes the PSCBS estimates and make such
decisions, but that is not part of PSCBS itself.

You can always manual adjust negative estimates to be zero, if you
really need them not to be negative, but I still haven't had to do it.

/Henrik

>
> However it stopped reading in Celfiles after 2,246 files after about 11

Ouch, I hope I'm not about to loose my "20,000 CEL file" bet ;)
...but I'm sure there is a simple explanation.

>
>
> The code used was as follows:
>
> setwd("path")
> library(aroma.affymetrix)
> verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8, timestamp=TRUE)
> chipType <- "HG-U133A"
> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType(chipType)
> print(cdf)
> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("CELFILES", cdf=cdf)
> print(cs)
> bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
> csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose)
>
>
> The code appears to conclude but on inspection it only placed 2,246 files in
> the output probeData/ folder.

First of all, what does/did print(cs) it report?  More precisely, does
it report 5,000 files, or could it be that it actually only reports
2,246 files?

Second, if there is a problem, key to troubleshoot it is to know what
you mean by "conclude".  Did process() return to the R prompt as if it
was successfully completed?  If so what did/does print(csBC) return
afterwards?

Third, if there was an *error* in process(), it is very useful to see
the last 20-50 lines of verbose output, because that will help narrow
down where things go havoc.  Also, whenever getting an *error*, first
thing to do is always to call troubleshoot() to see where the error
occurs.

Finally, does it help if you restart R and rerun your script?  FYI,
the already processed 2,246 files are still there and will be skipped,
so it shouldn't take too long.

/Henrik
